translation_updates.summary: Robert Remak (1815–1865) was an embryologist, physiologist and neurologist, born in Posen, Prussia, who is credited with discovering that cells originate by the division of pre-existing cells. He reached the conclusion by observing dividing red blood cells in chicken embryos and then confirming the same pattern in every frog egg immediately after fertilization. The article reports, attributing the assessment to the historian Paul Weindling, that Rudolf Virchow plagiarized this notion from him; the attribution is recorded here as the source states it, not adjudicated. Remak is also known for reducing Karl Ernst von Baer's four germ layers to the three still used today.

James Clerk Maxwell (1831–1879) was a Scottish physicist and mathematician whose classical theory of electromagnetic radiation was the first to describe electricity, magnetism and light as manifestations of one phenomenon — an achievement the article calls the second great unification in physics after Newton's. He was also key in the creation of statistical mechanics, and the first to derive the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution describing the kinetic theory of gases. In 1871 he returned to Cambridge as the first Cavendish Professor of Physics, overseeing construction of the Cavendish Laboratory, and the article regards him as a founder of the modern field of electrical engineering.

Josiah Willard Gibbs (1839–1903) was an American mechanical engineer and scientist who made fundamental theoretical contributions to physics, chemistry and mathematics. Together with James Clerk Maxwell and Ludwig Boltzmann he created statistical mechanics — a term he coined — explaining the laws of thermodynamics as consequences of the statistical properties of ensembles of a system's possible states. His work applying thermodynamics is described as instrumental in transforming physical chemistry into a rigorous deductive science, and as a mathematician he created modern vector calculus independently of Oliver Heaviside.

Hendrik Lorentz (1853–1928) was a Dutch theoretical physicist who shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman for their discovery and theoretical explanation of the Zeeman effect. He derived the Lorentz transformation of the special theory of relativity, as well as the Lorentz force describing the force on a charged particle in an electromagnetic field. The article states that in 1905 Einstein used many of the concepts, mathematical tools and results Lorentz had discussed in writing the paper known today as special relativity — influence on the theory rather than authorship of it. Lorentz was also one of the few scientists who supported Einstein's search for general relativity from the beginning.

Alfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) was an English mathematician and philosopher. With his former student Bertrand Russell he wrote the three-volume Principia Mathematica (1910–1913), considered one of the twentieth century's most important works in mathematical logic. He created the philosophical school known as process philosophy, arguing that reality consists of processes rather than material objects and that processes are best defined by their relations with other processes; his Process and Reality is regarded as that school's foundational text.

According to historian Paul Weindling, Rudolf Virchow, one of the founders of modern cell theory, plagiarized Remak's notion that all cells come from pre-existing cells.
He is best known for reducing Karl Ernst von Baer's four germ layers to three: the ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
